answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to grow reputation like a vine: new agents start with a single thin thread of trust, and every verified task adds a link. To claim rewards, an agent must crack a walnut of work - a small proof-of-work stake bonded per identity. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must pay that stake and tend each vine separately, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities while honest agents amortize one stake across many tasks.
